title: A bare write on a short-lived bun:sqlite connection can silently not land, so every corrupt-on-disk test rests on an unverified premise
description:
FILED 2026-09-29 from WCLI-57, which observed it and deliberately did not touch it: the failing tree was byte-identical to a passing one, and the change under test was a CI trigger.

THE INSTANCE. Run 36592695262, the push run for de3439b (the dev tip after opum-ai/ward-cli#116 merged). The Check job went red on the vault-store case that replaces the ciphertext on disk and requires the read to fail closed: Expected vault_authentication_failed, Received not-a-ward-error. That tree is byte-identical to 463c264 (both 611b296d), whose pull_request run 36592546690 passed all three contexts; re-running the failed job unchanged (attempt 2) returned success; and this run had the runner group to itself, so the duplication WCLI-57 removed is not its cause.

WHAT THE VALUE MEANS. The test helper's codeOf returns not-a-ward-error when the call did not throw at all, so the store returned the ORIGINAL plaintext from a vault whose ciphertext was supposed to have just been randomised.

REPRODUCED, THEN ATTRIBUTED BY CONSTRUCTION (bun 1.3.14, macOS, this session):
- The failing shape, 300 iterations: 1 iteration read the original plaintext; a raw read-back of the file showed the bytes UNCHANGED, and a second identical UPDATE landed.
- 600 iterations: 3 silent non-landings, each of which landed on a retry, with no journal file present.
- CONTROL WITH NO WARD CODE INVOLVED (bare bun:sqlite: create and insert on one short-lived connection, a bare UPDATE on a second, a read-back on a third): 800 iterations, 1 silent non-landing. The mechanism is bun:sqlite's and the store's read was correct in every observed case.
- WARD'S OWN WRITE PATH: 400 iterations of create and mutate, each through a fresh store object over a short-lived connection, read back through another: 0 losses. At the measured rate this bounds the exposure rather than ruling it out, and that limit is the honest reading.

EXPOSURE. The raw helper's mutation is the premise of every case that corrupts the file and then asserts a refusal: the ciphertext-authentication case, the three altered-layout alterations, and the seven oversized or malformed stored-field tampers. A mutation that does not land fails those cases for a reason unrelated to the code under test; in the other direction the same mechanism would let a case pass while testing nothing at all.

REMEDY SHAPE, proposed rather than decided: make a non-landing mutation impossible to mistake for a result - verify the file bytes actually changed and retry (a retry landed every time here), or read back inside the helper and fail with a message that names the harness rather than the vault. Whether the bun:sqlite behaviour itself warrants a report to its owners is this task's call, not an assumption carried in from here.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every case that mutates the vault on disk and then asserts an outcome either verifies its mutation took effect or is shown immune to a silent non-landing write, so a non-landing write can no longer be read as a result about the code.

A loop of the reproduced shape - short-lived connection, bare autocommit UPDATE, fresh-connection read-back - at a size at least as large as those recorded here produces no silent non-landing write through the helper, or the residual rate and its consequence are recorded.

The affected shape is characterised by measurement rather than by analogy: whether it is specifically a bare exec immediately followed by close, and whether the store's own transactional write path shares it, are answered from evidence.
